summary: No clean single-figure willingness-to-pay VSL was extractable for Brazil; the recent hedonic-wage study (PNS 2019, quantile regression with sample-selection correction) reports a Value of Statistical Injury rather than a headline VSL, so Brazil is flagged as not yet anchorable.
label_raw: Brazilian hedonic-wage VSI (PNS 2019) - no headline VSL
source_citation: ResearchGate 'Inequality and the Value of a Statistical Life'; Brazilian hedonic-wage paper using PNS 2019. Not yet anchorable - needs direct primary-source fetch before use.

summary: Best hedonic-wage value of a statistical life for Chile (Heckit 2SLS correcting endogeneity/selection; CASEN 2013 + occupational-risk records), US$3.73M (2013 USD) normalized to ~$5.0M (2024 USD), 95% CI US$3.4M-4.0M; revealed-preference WTP anchor and the high end of this sample.
source_citation: Mardones & Riquelme (2018), Latin American Research Review. https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/latin-american-research-review/article/estimation-of-the-value-of-statistical-life-in-chile-and-extrapolation-to-other-latin-american-countries/5F9D844230E591849C0AA11BD4527A19 (2013->2024 CPI x1.34, researcher arithmetic)

summary: Contingent-valuation (WTP) value of a statistical life from six representative Chinese cities to reduce air-pollution death risk, CNY 4.76M = ~US$690,000 (2019) normalized to ~$830,000 (2024 USD); WTP construct, not compensation.
source_citation: Chinese Journal of Population, Resources and Environment (2023). https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2325426223000530 (USD-conversion-year uncertain; researcher arithmetic)

summary: Stated-preference (payment-card WTP) value of a statistical life for urban Chinese residents (Shanghai, Nanning, Jiujiang), ~$615,000 in 2016 USD normalized to ~$800,000 (2024 USD); this is ex ante willingness-to-pay for a 5-in-10,000 annual mortality-risk reduction, not ex post compensation.
source_citation: Hoffmann, Krupnick & Qin (2017), Journal of Benefit-Cost Analysis, 'Building a Set of Internationally Comparable VSL Studies: Estimates of Chinese Willingness to Pay to Reduce Mortality Risk'. https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/journal-of-benefit-cost-analysis/article/building-a-set-of-internationally-comparable-value-of-statistical-life-studies-estimates-of-chinese-willingness-to-pay-to-reduce-mortality-risk/F0736C663CC8C30263752C6E7D187526 (2016->2024 CPI x1.30, researcher arithmetic)

summary: Hedonic-wage (compensating wage differential, revealed-preference) value of a statistical life for blue-collar male manufacturing workers in Ahmedabad, Gujarat, INR 44.69M = ~$0.64M (2018 USD) normalized to ~$0.80M (2024 USD); WTP-type anchor, not compensation.
source_citation: 'Value of statistical life in India: A hedonic wage approach' (Madheswaran-style), IDEAS/RePEc working paper. https://ideas.repec.org/p/sch/wpaper/407.html (benefit-transfer cross-checks give wider $0.5-1.6M range; USD-year basis uncertain)

summary: Benefit-transfer value of a statistical life for Mexico, US$2.0M base (2021 USD) normalized to ~$2.3M (2024 USD) with a sub-national range of $0.4M (Chiapas) to $3.3M (Mexico City); extrapolated downward from an OECD VSL of $9M with income elasticity 1.0, so it is not an independent primary national estimate.
source_citation: Becerra-Perez et al. (2024), Int. J. Environmental Research and Public Health, PMC11032065. https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11032065/ (OECD benefit-transfer, income elasticity 1.0; 2021->2024 CPI x1.16, researcher arithmetic)

summary: Primary wage-risk (compensating wage differential) value of a statistical life for Mexico City metro workers (~600 workers, perceived and actuarial occupational risk), US$235,000-325,000 (2002 USD) normalized to ~$410,000-565,000 (2024 USD); the genuine primary Mexican WTP/wage-risk anchor (recorded at the ~$490k midpoint).
source_citation: Hammitt & Ibarraran (2006), Health Economics. https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/hec.1137 (2002->2024 CPI x1.74, researcher arithmetic; 2024-USD midpoint of $410k-$565k range)

summary: Survey/opinion-poll 'cost of financial compensation for death' for Russia, ~$71,500 (early 2015) normalized to ~$94,000 (2024 USD), with a broader literature range of $40,000-$2,000,000; journalistic secondary source, included only to bracket the low end of the WTP spectrum.
label_raw: ~$71,500 (2015) cost of financial compensation for death
source_citation: The Bell, 'The value of a Russian life' (journalistic secondary source citing Russian polling). https://en.thebell.io/the-value-of-a-russian-life/ (not peer-reviewed; flag for replacement with academic source)

summary: Implied 'value of a death averted' (VSL proxy) for South Africa derived from health-spending elasticity on the age-standardised death rate, ZAR 1.89M (2020) ~ US$120,000-130,000 (2024 USD); this is a government revealed/supply-side valuation via budget, not stated willingness-to-pay, making it a methodologically weaker WTP anchor.
label_raw: ZAR 1.472M (2015) / ZAR 1.89M (2020) value of a death averted
source_citation: Edoka & Stacey (health-spending elasticity), cited in Barr et al., South African Journal of Economic and Management Sciences (2023, alcohol cost-benefit analysis). https://sajems.org/index.php/sajems/article/view/5314/2956 (implied value, ZAR1.89M 2020 at ~16.5/USD then CPI-adjusted)

summary: Updated hedonic log-wage value of a statistical life for Thailand (national labour-force survey + workplace-risk data 2014-2021), US$2,015,694 (2021, PPP-adjusted); PPP basis means it is not directly comparable to the market-exchange-rate figures.
source_citation: Journal of Applied Economics and Management Strategy. http://kuojs.lib.ku.ac.th/index.php/jaems/article/view/6254 (PPP-adjusted; stated as 2021 PPP USD)

summary: Hedonic-wage value of a statistical life for Thailand (Labour Force Survey + Social Security Office, 2012-2014 averaged), mean $1.21M (2011 USD) normalized to ~$1.7M (2024 USD), with income elasticity 1.488 (income-elastic); revealed-preference WTP anchor.
label_raw: Mean VSL $1.21M / median $0.66M (2011 USD), income elasticity 1.488
source_citation: Witvorapong & Komonpaisarn (2020), Journal of Consumer Policy. https://ideas.repec.org/a/kap/jcopol/v43y2020i3d10.1007_s10603-019-09431-2.html (2011->2024 CPI x1.41, researcher arithmetic)
